Choose luggage around the trip and airline limits

Measure the outside, including wheels and handles

Compare the airline's current allowance with the complete case dimensions and empty weight. A manufacturer's cabin-size label is not universal airline approval. Expandable sections can move a packed case outside the limit. If you travel with several airlines, check the most restrictive journey rather than choosing the largest nominal capacity.

Check the parts you will handle repeatedly

Look at wheel layout, handle adjustment, opening style and access to contents in a small hotel room. A clamshell case needs a different floor space from a top-opening bag. For a set, confirm which case sizes you would actually use. Warranty coverage, replacement wheels and zipper support can be more useful than an extra unused piece. No shell material alone guarantees that checked luggage will arrive undamaged.
